layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrochemical and immersion tests have been applied to a study of the localized corrosion resistance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of two molybdenum-bearing nickel alloys, Alloys C-276 and 625, in neutral chloride solutions in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature range of 25 to 200 C as part of the container materials evaluation screening tests for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Canadian Nuclear Fuel Waste Management Program. Cyclic polarization studies show that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passivation breakdown potentials move rapidly to more active values with increasing temperatures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicating a reduced resistance to localized corrosion. The results of immersion tests show that both

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys do suffer crevice corrosion in neutrai aerated sodium chloride solutions at elevated temperatures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but that in both cases, there is a limiting temperature >100 C, below which, the alloys are not attacked,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regardless of the chloride concentration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two molybdenum-bearing nickel alloys, Alloys C-276 and 625, were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: included in the group of passive alloys identified by Nuttall and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Urbanic as possible candidate container materials for the Canadian

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nuclear Fuel Waste Management Program. The concept being

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assessed involves the disposal of nuclear waste by deep burial in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Canadian Shield. The deep groundwaters of the Canadian Shield

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: may have a high chloride content,² and the possibilíty of passivation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: breakdown and subsequent localized corrosion (crevice and/or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting) of any passive metals considered for the containers must be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The assessment of materials by Nuttall and Urbanic' revealed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a paucity of data for the localized corrosion of nickel alloys in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range of temperature and chloride content expected in a disposal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vault. At that time, it was assumed for the purpose of assessment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "that the container temperature will be 150 C or less." However, more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recently, the maximum container-skin temperature specified³ for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concept assessment engineering studies is 100 C.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it is likely that oxygen will be present initially as a result of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: burial operations and, subsequently, as a result of radiolysis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The present study, which involved electrochemical and immer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion tests, was conducted to determine the conditions (temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and chloride content) required to stimulate localized corrosion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys C-276 and 625. It was decided to use a wide range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperatures, 25 to 200 C, and NaCi concentrations of 0.1 wt% to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: saturation so that the results may assist in the understanding of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mechanism of the localized corrosion, rather than simply obtain data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for specific concept assessment guidelines.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An understanding of the mechanism would be required to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results to very long exposure times, as discussed later.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: construct the mathematical models necessary to extrapolate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The test specimens were machined from plate of a composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grade.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two types of specimens were used:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Plain blocks, 11 x 11 x 7 mm thick, with a drilled and tapped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connection, used as electrodes with a polytetrafluorethylene (PTFE)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Blocks, 25 x 13 x 7 mm thick, fitted with a radially grooved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 16-mm diameter PTFE washer assembly bolted to the block with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bolt made from the alloy under test. A plain PTFE backing washer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 16-mm diameter was used. A torque of 6 Nm was used. Some of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these specimens had a drilled and tapped connection and were used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as electrodes; the others were used for the immersion tests.

layout_dets.text: Results and Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrochemical Studies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The cyclic potentiodynamic polarization method was used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: determine the susceptibility of the alloys to localized corrosion. Both

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plain and creviced specimens were used in the initial experiments. it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was subseguently found unnecessary to use a crevice assembly in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the electrochemical tests, since in every case where localized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion occurred at the artificial crevice assembly, it also occurred

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the PTFE compression gasket located at the electrode mount.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Perhaps, it is not surprising that Asphahani⁶ coined the term

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: damaging potential to describe passivation breakdown potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rather than using the terms pitting potentials or crevice potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: since it is difficult to distinguish between these two forms of attack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with cyclic polarization tests. Indeed, the round robin tests? con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ducted in conjunction with the standard cyclic polarization test,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ASTM(2) Standard G-61, illustrated this fact very well, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standard test makes no attempt to distinguish between pitting and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The three conditions that were observed (Figures 1 and 2) when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the electrodes were subsequently examined were passivation main-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tained with no corrosion, crevice corrosion at the PTFE electrode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mount, and crevice corrosion at the PTFE electrode mount plus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting on the freely exposed surfaces. On this basis, Alloy C-276

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: displayed superior resistance to localized corrosion than Alloy 625.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The cyclic polarization test for localized corrosion is a severe test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involving the polarization of a metal to potentials that may not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieved under natural corrosion conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: At high temperatures, the alloys exhibited classical hysteresis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: loops [Figures 3(a) and (b)], characteristic of passivation breakdown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the upward sweep and repassivation on the downward sweep.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Under these conditions, passivation breakdown potentials,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repassivation potentials (sometimes called the protection potential),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could be readily obtained from the polarization curves. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conversion of the potentials to the SHE(T) scale was achieved using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the method given by Macdonald;º the thermal junction potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were assumed to be negligible.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beside each data point is the exposure time in days; (•)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion with obvious metal loss, (o) no corro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion, and (- - - - -) tentative crevice temperature envelope.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Oldfield-Sutton model was successfully applied to a study of crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion of SS in seawater by Kain,2º where again, the major effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the bulk concentration of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is illustrated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On the basis of the Oldfield-Sutton model, it must be assumed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that either the exposure times at the low chloride concentrations were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: too short or else the critical crevice solution could not be attained at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any exposure time at the lower temperatures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Oldfield and Sutton did not consider either breakdown or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protection potentials to be appropriate parameters for inclusion in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their crevice corrosion model, although their experimental results²1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with AISI 316 SS showed a potential/time relationship characteristic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of passivation breakdown obtained when the breakdown potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theory is applied,17 albeit at potentials lower than those normally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associated with the passivation breakdown of AlSI 316 SS. Further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the initial stages of the attack were said to take the form of micropits,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which only later coalesced to give active dissolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ni Alloys and Nuclear Waste Containers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: If the existence of a limiting crevice corrosion temperature for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys C-276 and 625 above 100 C is confirmed, the molybdenum-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bearing nickel alloys would be strong candidates for further consid-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eration for nuclear waste disposal containers. The significance of this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limiting temperature is that possible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration at the canister

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface, because of boiling before the full hydrostatic pressure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: develops, would not cause a problem in terms of localized corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The recent evaluation of corrosion screening tests conducted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the Commission of the European Communities²²concluded that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the molybdenum-bearing nickel alloys exhibited good resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion in chloride solutions, with Alloy C-276 ranked higher than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloy 625, although the nickel alloy selected for further study, Alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C-4, did suffer crevice corrosion at 90 C in a MgCl₂-rich brine under

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gamma radiation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Clearly, the type of data presented here, which was intended to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fill a gap in our knowledge and understanding of the localized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion behavior of molybdenum-bearing nickel alloys, must be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supplemented by more extensive long-term testing. And as pointed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: out by Accary,²² further experimental studies should be paralleled by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: further development of the mathematical modeling of the type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CORROSION—NACE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: developed by Oldfield and Sutton19,21 and used by Kain.2º No

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion model presently exists that would allow for the prediction of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: localized corrosion over the containment durations involved in waste

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disposal, especially if long-term factors, such as solid state diffusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leading to aging of alloys and penetration of environmental elements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into the alloy, or loss of its components, are to be taken into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: account.22

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Not withstanding the difficulties in such modeling, such an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach is required so that medium to long-term (10 to 50 year) pilot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests can be extrapolated to the 500 year desired minimum container

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effectiveness.
